title: Transient SSO session claim race causing permission denial and stale elevated access
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers reported two related but opposite RBAC failures after recent RBAC v2 + SSO claim changes: (1) operations that should be allowed returned permission denied, and (2) short-lived administrative actions were recorded as performed by users who later retained elevated access (stale over-permission). Both were triggered around SSO re-auth/refresh flows when session claims were updated concurrently with role mapping reconciliation. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, patch, tests, and rollout for a targeted hotfix and mitigations.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use a user that is in an external SAML group mapped to 'viewer' but intermittently promoted via an SSO attribute to 'temp-admin' during session refresh.
2) Trigger a session refresh (re-sso/assertion) while making API calls that require 'viewer' permissions (e.g., read logs) and admin actions (e.g., change project quota).
3) Observe cases where read requests fail with permission denied for a short window, and separately where admin actions succeed but the session later lacks admin in the role lookup cache yet audit shows the action attributed to the elevated role.
4) Reproduce under varying timing and with multiple concurrent requests to amplify race window.
investigation_summary: We reproduced locally and in a debug customer environment. Core subsystems implicated: SSO assertion handler, RBAC v2 role resolution cache, session claim propagation, and audit-logging attribution. Timing: when an assertion-based role hint arrives while a background role reconciliation loop is updating RBAC mappings, concurrent requests hit mixed state: the request path sometimes reads an in-memory claim blob that includes the temporary 'admin' hint while the authoritative role index hasn't finished reconciliation, leading to either a transient denial (because policy evaluation path used the old mapping) or to logging of admin-scoped actions against a session that later lost admin rights but audit recorded the elevated principal. We observed two distinct bugs: (A) non-atomic swap of session claim -> role-lookup key causing mismatched evaluation, (B) audit attribution uses cached claim snapshot rather than authoritative role resolution at time of request completion.
findings:
- Root cause A: session.claims update and role_index.update are not serialized: a request can observe a claim without corresponding role_index entries, which makes policy evaluator fall back to more restrictive default (permission denied).
- Root cause B: audit service records role names from the ephemeral claim snapshot at request start but does not validate against role_index at commit time, allowing a stale elevated entry to be recorded after role revocation/rollback.
- Race window is small (~50-300ms under heavy load) but reproducible with concurrent refreshes.
- Affected flows: SAML assertion-linked attribute changes, group-syncs that change mapping, manual role patches during active sessions.
- Not a database corruption issue; confined to in-memory ordering and caching logic.
proposed_fix:
1) Make session-claim -> role-resolution an atomic handoff: introduce a single update path that updates both the session claim blob and the derived role-index entry under the same lock or via a compare-and-swap token.
2) Change policy evaluator to consult the authoritative role-index by default; only use session claim hints as an optimization if a consistency token confirms index is current.
3) For audit logging, record both the ephemeral claim snapshot and a resolved authoritative role set at time of request commit, and add a reconciliation step to mark audit entries that were based on transient claims.
4) Add a short-lived fallback that, on detection of inconsistent claim/index versions, retries evaluation once after index stable, to reduce customer-facing denials.
5) Backport minimal runtime fix and add integration tests.
patch_reference: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876 - 'rbac: atomic session claim-to-index update and audit reconciliation' (draft)
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (hotfix): Deploy runtime-1.22.hotfix (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours) with guardrails: feature-flagged atomic update enabled only for RBAC-v2 customers with SAML attribute mapping. Monitor error rates and audit mismatches.
Phase 2: enable optimistic fast-path for all customers after 72h if metrics stable.
Phase 3: full rollout and backfill audit reconciliation for the last 72h of traffic.
Rollback: disable feature-flag and return to previous code path. We will also temporarily throttle concurrent SSO assertion processing for impacted customers during rollout window as a mitigation.
monitoring_and_metrics: Add/track: 1) rbac.eval.permission_denied_rate (filter by reason=claim-index-mismatch), 2) audit.reconciliation.mismatch_count, 3) sso.refresh_concurrent_count, 4) request.retry_after_index_stable_count. Set alert: if permission_denied_rate increases >5x baseline for >10m during canary, pause rollout. Dashboards: create RBAC-Races board and add customer-specific filters (customer_id).
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for atomic update, mock role_index delays to simulate race. Integration tests: stress test with concurrent SSO refresh + API calls asserting no permission-denied spikes and correct audit attribution. End-to-end scenario on staging using customer-replay traces (sanitized), verify audit reconciliation backfill works and does not duplicate audit entries. Add chaos tests that pause role_index update threads.
postmortem_notes: Customer escalations: two customers (acct: acme-bio, acct: fintech-svc) reported blocking behavior; we mitigated with temporary throttling and manual audit correction. We will run a targeted full audit reconciliation for last 7 days of traffic for both customers and offer remediation. Root cause classification: concurrency bug in RBAC v2 integration with SSO claim hints. Prevent recurrence: require serialization contract for any future optimization that uses ephemeral claims.
